claims.statement: UOKiK lists unjustified reductions of amounts due after accepted delivery among prohibited practices in agricultural and food supply relationships.
UOKiK says certain marketing, advertising, storage and display charges are allowed only when clearly and unambiguously agreed in advance, making contract-to-charge evidence operationally relevant.
UOKiK documented a case in which price or quantity discrepancies held back payment for an entire delivery and prolonged resolution, and the buyer committed to change disputed-invoice handling.

contrary_evidence: UOKiK enforcement protects public interests and does not itself compensate an individual supplier, so software evidence does not assure recovery.
Large suppliers already run sophisticated trade-promotion and deduction teams; the wedge is the underserved mid-market.

economics.acquisition_route: Outsourced finance partners run a no-recovery-no-fee three-month remittance audit, then convert successful clients to monitoring
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 100 suppliers at 48,000 PLN recurring ARR plus 1.5-3m PLN annual recovery fees yields 6-8m PLN revenue by years 4-6. Productization to 20%+ margin and majority ownership could create over 5m PLN founder net worth in years 5-7.
economics.founder_time: 15-22 hours weekly at launch; use independent former supplier-finance specialists for review and avoid current-employer overlap
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 60-78% during managed launch, rising to 78-88% as retailer/reason-code automation improves
economics.payback: Hypothesis: under 3 months when first recoveries fund acquisition; 6-9 months if clients demand subscription-only pricing
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 2,000-8,000 PLN monthly plus 8-15% of verified cash recoveries; fixed-fee prevention tier after six months
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every retailer remittance and promotion cycle repeats; contract and outcome history make future disputes cheaper and faster

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Retailer-specific deduction taxonomy, contract-clause mappings and anonymized resolution outcomes reveal which evidence closes each reason code fastest
fingerprint.customer: Polish small and mid-sized food/FMCG suppliers selling through large retailers and wholesalers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Outsourced CFO/accounting firms, ERP implementers, food-industry associations and receivables insurers refer suppliers at the moment cash leakage is visible
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Managed recovery audit evolving into retailer-specific deduction SaaS, with monthly subscription and bounded success fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Supplier pays a subscription for ongoing deduction monitoring and a success fee only when a documented accounting discrepancy is recovered
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A retailer remittance is below the invoiced amount or a rebate/marketing fee lacks a clear contractual and performance link

founder_fit: FMCG context and quantitative reconciliation provide unusually strong founder insight if confidentiality is protected.
A service-first audit is low-capital and measurable.
Partner referrals and document workflows minimize camera/public-brand demands.
risks: Current employment in FMCG creates conflict-of-interest and confidentiality risks requiring explicit boundaries.
Success-fee services can drift into legal advice unless scope and referrals are clear.
Retailers may retaliate commercially even when a supplier has a valid claim.

structure.control_point: Supplier acceptance or dispute of a retailer remittance deduction and promotion accrual close
structure.critical_dependency: Access to contracts and operational evidence, plus strict separation from legal representation and from the founder's employer-confidential information

thesis: Offer smaller Polish food and FMCG suppliers a recovery and prevention layer for retailer deductions, quantity/price disputes, rebates and marketing charges. It ingests contracts, orders, proof of delivery, invoices, remittances and promotion evidence; separates valid deductions from unsupported ones; and produces a factual claim packet for the supplier's own finance/legal approval. Start as a contingency-priced reconciliation service, then productize retailer-specific reason codes and sell through outsourced finance teams, ERP implementers and industry associations. It is not a law firm and should exclude any employer-confidential logic or data.
title: FMCG Retailer Deduction Resolver
uncertainties: Recoverable deduction value among suppliers small enough to outsource
Availability and quality of promotion-performance evidence
Whether industry associations will endorse a neutral service
